title: Shift-loop reachability
statement: Let $E,B\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathcal O$ assign a Boolean answer to each of four indices and each Boolean word, let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $k$ be one of the three shift operations, and let $\mathrm{st}$ be an 18-register machine state. Suppose every register of $\mathrm{st}$ is at most $B$, its scratch register $Z$ is zero, and the value of the register associated with $k$, multiplied by $2^C$, is at most $B$. Then the machine has a finite run from phase zero at the shift operation $k$ to its exit label, ending with that register equal to its initial value multiplied by $2^C$ and the loop counter $C$ equal to zero; every configuration strictly before the endpoint satisfies the machine guard with bound $B$.

replaced:
Let $E,B\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathcal O$ be an oracle assigning a Boolean answer to each
of four indices and each Boolean word, let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $k$ be one of the
three shift operations, and let $\mathrm{st}$ be a state of the 18-register machine.
Suppose every register of $\mathrm{st}$ is at most $B$, its scratch register $Z$ is
zero, and the value of the register acted on by $k$, multiplied by $2^{C}$, is at most
$B$. Then the machine can reach the exit label for $k$ from label $k$ at phase zero,
with the register acted on by $k$ multiplied by $2^C$ and the loop counter $C$ cleared;
throughout the run, every intermediate configuration before the final one satisfies the
machine guard with bound $B$.
